weaknesses.title: Central proof is a black-box computation resting on unverified assumptions
weaknesses.detail: Theorem 1 rests on Theorem 5.1 of D'Hoker–Kaidi and on 'the standard lemma' (a harmonic, SL(2,Z)-invariant function of polynomial growth is constant), and neither is checked or re-proved. The decisive step 3 is only described: the Laurent polynomials of the individual C(a,b,c) and their rational-arithmetic combination are not shown, even for one weight such as w=9 or 11. The only cross-check mentioned, against eq. (5.19), covers the terms that carry no zeta products. That is a consistency check on the other terms, not on the τ2^0 coefficient that carries the claim. The reader cannot verify that this coefficient equals g_w ζ(w) without re-running the repository. Calling this a 'proof' is therefore weak for a mathematical-physics journal.
weaknesses.suggestion: Write out the Laurent computation explicitly for at least w=9 and w=11, including the contribution of each C(a,b,c) to the τ2^0 term. State the lemma and the exact hypotheses of D'Hoker–Kaidi Thm 5.1 as used. Justify the polynomial-growth and invariance claims for the combination, and give an independent check of the τ2^0 coefficient.

weaknesses.title: Overclaim in the title and abstract relative to what is established, and unclear novelty
weaknesses.detail: The title promises 'closed forms for the constants', but the formula is proved only for odd 3≤w≤61. It is checked numerically only up to w=17, and a general proof is declared open (Remark 1, open question (i)). The 'Conjecture 1' label inside a Remark is confusing, and Fig. 2 still calls the formula 'conjectured'. Novelty is muddled. The w=3, 5, 7 cases and the combinations are known, and g7 appears in the literature. The text says DGV eq. 3.34 'writes' g9 but then says g9 is not given there. Because the contribution is a finite-range computation of known objects, the claimed advance is unclear.
weaknesses.suggestion: Retitle and reword the abstract to say 'a closed form conjectured from data and proved for odd w≤61'. Move Conjecture 1 into a proper statement. Fix the contradictory sentence about g9. Add a table separating known results (w=3, 5, 7, and g9 if applicable) from new ones (w≥9 or 11).

weaknesses.title: X_w and the normalisations are not explicitly defined; Theorem 2 lacks supporting detail
weaknesses.detail: X_w is defined only as 'the DGV combination', and its coefficients are never given for general w. Propositions 1 and 2 use differently scaled combinations. For w=9 the combination has Δ = 288E(9), whereas Theorem 2 with f9=8 would give 576. For w=11 the Prop. 2 combination (Δ = 100E(11)) and Observation 1 (coefficients 19008 and so on) differ from X11 by unstated factors (about 36 for w=11 and 2 for w=9). Theorem 2 claims dimension 1 or 0 for w≤25. The paper does not say which basis of C(a,b,c) is used, nor how the linear conditions or the 'algebraic Laplace representation' are set up, nor whether linear independence of the C(a,b,c) is assumed. The reader cannot reproduce the statements from the text.
weaknesses.suggestion: Give the explicit formula or coefficients of X_w and the scale factor relative to the Prop./Obs. combinations (a table for w≤13 suffices). Describe the Laplace-algebra setup and the basis used for Theorem 2. State the normalisation consistently so that ΔX_w = w(w−1)f_w E(w) can be checked directly against Props 1 and 2.

weaknesses.title: Numerical evidence is thin and has unexplained or weakened elements
weaknesses.detail: Table 2 reports maximal residuals around 1e-43, yet the working precision is 32 digits. Residuals below the precision floor are unexplained, since the Fourier sums are truncated. Only 4 points are used. The Laplace-type checks rely on finite differences (h=1e-6) with a weak 1e-14 tolerance. The completeness claim for the weight-11 basis (Observation 2) failed its preregistered criterion, because the smallest other singular value, 4.1e-9, was below 1e-8. It was rescued by a second criterion set after the data were seen. The singular-value gaps shrink quickly with weight (0.73 → 8.6e-7 at w=9), so rank decisions are fragile. A precision-independent bug was found at τ1=1/4, which raises doubts about the evaluator beyond the 8 hardening points. The adversarial counter-check count (4 passed, 48 failed, 1 not executable) is confusing.
weaknesses.suggestion: Explain how residuals of 1e-43 are possible at 32 digits, or re-run with higher precision and more points, including points off τ1=1/4. Tone down the completeness claim for Observation 2, state clearly that the criterion was changed post hoc, and say that this is numerical evidence only. Clarify how the counter-checks were scored.

weaknesses.title: Unfocused scope, off-topic material and weakly supported process claims
weaknesses.detail: The paper includes content unrelated to the main result: Theorem 3 on eta-quotient spans for M4(Γ0(N)), Sturm-certified theta/j identities, weight-6 negative results, and a list of Laplace equations for C(2,1,1), C(2,2,1) and C(3,1,1) cited as already known. Process narration (17 rounds, agent roles, preregistration, a 'novelty search of 33 abstracts') takes the place of mathematical content. Claims such as 'not found in a targeted search of 33 abstracts' are not meaningful novelty evidence. Reference [5] is cited for Γ0(4) identities that have nothing to do with the main result. The automatically generated provenance appendix (the table with 'computed_rigorous/observed' levels) is not interpretable as printed. This dilutes the contribution and makes it hard to see which claims are essential.
weaknesses.suggestion: Cut the eta-quotient and Sturm material and the workflow narrative, or move them to supplementary material. Keep the appendix to the numerical methods and error control that support Theorems 1 and 2. Replace the novelty-search remarks with a proper comparison to the literature, and explain the provenance levels or drop that table.
